title: Slow Enough to Notice
headline: Why Hurry Kills Gratitude
tagline: A hurried heart rarely notices grace.
seo_title: Why Hurry Kills Gratitude: Psalm 103 and a Gratitude Walk | TheWrkShop
seo_description: One of the greatest enemies of gratitude isn't suffering; it's hurry. A practice for men built on Psalm 103:1-5: slow down, notice and give thanks.
verse_text: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all His benefits.

scriptures.text: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all His benefits.

items: One of the greatest enemies of gratitude isn’t suffering.
It’s hurry.
A hurried heart rarely notices grace.
It rushes from one responsibility to the next.
One achievement to another.
One goal to another.
Without ever stopping long enough to recognize what God has already done.
This is why Jesus often withdrew to lonely places to pray.
Not because He lacked purpose.
But because He refused to let busyness replace communion with His Father.
Gratitude grows where awareness grows.
And awareness requires margin.
Today, slow your pace.
Leave your phone behind if possible.
Walk without headphones.
Walk without an agenda.
Simply walk with God.
Notice your breathing.
Notice the people God has placed in your life.
Notice His provision, His protection, His patience, His kindness.
Notice His presence.
Then simply begin thanking Him.
Not because everything is perfect.
But because He has never stopped being good.
David doesn’t merely praise God.
He speaks to his own soul.
Notice those words: forget not.
The human heart remembers pain naturally.
It must intentionally remember grace.
Sometimes the soul needs to be reminded before it begins to rejoice.
What have I overlooked this week?
Where have I seen God’s fingerprints that I almost missed?
What ordinary moment is actually extraordinary when viewed through gratitude?
What if nothing changed in my circumstances this week…. except my awareness of God’s presence?

items: Train your heart to notice before it naturally complains.
Because what you repeatedly notice…. you eventually begin to treasure.
The grateful man doesn’t wait for extraordinary moments to worship.
He discovers that ordinary moments have been extraordinary all along.
Grace has been surrounding him the entire time.
He simply slowed down long enough to notice.
